selected_evidence.requirement: Every sudo command logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: Log file created, sudoers Defaults logfile/log_year config validated and installed, and entries captured showing 'Sep 5 00:05:xx 2026 : root/sudologtest : PWD=... USER=root ; COMMAND=...' for both root and a test user.

selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries kept out of the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: Defaults !syslog disabled sudo's syslog logging; COMMAND= line count in /var/log/auth.log stayed frozen at 7 (all pre-dating the config) across further sudo invocations, and /var/log/syslog had 0 COMMAND= entries throughout, while new sudo activity kept appearing only in the dedicated file.
Temporary NOPASSWD sudo user sudologtest created, sudo id run as that user logged with 'sudologtest' as the acting user, then user and temp sudoers file fully removed.
Captured boot_id bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49, uptime, active rsyslog, sudoers config content, and 24-line log file as pre-restart baseline.
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned acknowledgement before the connection dropped; immediate follow-up probe failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down for restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 17065b78-02a9-472a-ac2d-4cbb64e08146, differing from the pre-restart baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data (sudo command logging)
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, uptime -s showed a new boot time, rsyslog was active, the sudoers config file was intact, the log file persisted with prior entries plus new appended lines, and a fresh sudo command continued to log only to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with no new auth.log COMMAND= entries.
